metadata.benchmark: competitive_benchmark (Mercury vs PyOD, ADBench 47 Classical + 10 CV/NLP)
metadata.protocol: per dataset: stratified cap to 2*MAX_SAMPLES (seed 42); normal-only train half; test = remaining normals + all anomalies capped to MAX_SAMPLES; fixed-seed de-leak shuffle of test rows (batch-order leakage guard, applied to every method identically); StandardScaler fit on train only; library defaults for every method; no per-dataset tuning; unsupervised-fair (no method sees labels)
metadata.mercury_fusion_protocol: fit_fusion(X_train, y=None): label-free detector-consensus path; semi-supervised mode NOT used because PyOD baselines get no labels
metadata.deep_baselines_note: PyOD deep baselines (AutoEncoder) excluded: under the defaults-only, CPU-only, no-tuning budget they measure the budget cap rather than the method; see pyod_integration.DEFAULT_BASELINES
metadata.embedding_variant_note: CV/NLP corpora use one representative ADBench variant per source: _0 where per-class variants exist; MNIST-C_brightness / MVTec-AD_bottle (no _0 variant exists upstream); amazon/imdb/yelp ship a single file
